title: Stateless by default, one schema for what must persist

concept.heading: No session in memory; a migrated database for the facts that outlive a request
paragraphs: The 2026-07-28 spec made the server stateless so any copy can answer any request. That does not mean no database. Three things from earlier modules genuinely must outlive a request: pending approvals, idempotency keys already seen, and task handles. They were each created on the fly by their own store. This lesson gives them one home: a single SQLite file whose schema is created and evolved by numbered migration files.

A migration is a SQL file with a number. StateDB.migrate() applies the ones not yet recorded in schema_migrations, in order, each in its own transaction, and records the name. Run it on an empty file and you get the full schema; run it again and nothing happens; add 005_something.sql and only that applies. A client's laptop, a free host, and your machine all end up with the same tables, and a schema change is a reviewable file in git.

The connection context manager is the Python idea this lesson introduces: with db.connection() as conn commits when the block ends normally and rolls back when an exception escapes, so a half-written approval row cannot survive a crash in the middle of approve().
concept.lowCodeEquivalent: Dataverse tables with solution-managed schema changes: you never edited a production table by hand, you shipped a solution. Migrations are the solution file for SQLite.

pythonBlock.title: Python you need: context managers
pythonBlock.intro: @contextmanager turns a generator into a with-block: everything before yield is setup, after yield is teardown, and a finally runs even when the body raises.
pythonBlock.code:
from contextlib import contextmanager
import sqlite3

@contextmanager
def connection(self):
    conn = sqlite3.connect(self.db_path)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    try:
        yield conn          # the with-block body runs here
        conn.commit()       # normal exit
    except BaseException:
        conn.rollback()     # the body raised: undo everything
        raise
    finally:
        conn.close()

with db.connection() as conn:
    conn.execute("INSERT INTO schema_migrations (version, applied_at) VALUES (?, ?)", (name, now))

spec: Write migrations 001 to 004 per tools/migrations/README.md with the exact columns the Module 3 and 4 stores use (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS).
Implement StateDB: connection() as a commit/rollback context manager, migrate() with a schema_migrations ledger and one transaction per file, schema_version(), tables().
Point the three stores and the server at one STATE_DB path (keep APPROVALS_DB, TASKS_DB as overrides if you like) and run migrate() at server startup.
Delete your local state file, start the server, and confirm the tables appear from the migrations alone.
